newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-BULLISH DLR TO FACE CORRECTION PRESSURES.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-BULLISH DLR TO FACE CORRECTION PRESSURES.

text.p: Odds the dollar's rally will suffer a temporary correction are increasing even as the greenback fetched another set of new highs on Wednesday and key technical studies have yet to turn bearish, experts said.
Overbought conditions have become more pronounced and the dollar has shown worrisome volatility as it zeroed in on big longer-term targets at 1.90 marks and 120 yen, they said.
Darren Spain, global foreign exchange analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston Corp said for the first time in three months his rampant bullishness has started to fade.
"I'm not picking a top in the dollar. I'm wary of a healthy correction but I'm still bullish," Spain said. "For example, in my strategy, I've brought all my stop-reverses up tight."

In its advance to a near 3-month high at 119.58 yen on Wednesday, the dollar fell just short of the 119.75 chart target and psychological resistance at 120, where dealers are expected to get nervous about intervention.
A stab at 121 yen -- the .618 retracement of the 127.45 to 110.60 slide this year -- is still possible but analysts said negative technicals could start to kick in by then.
"You have 120 yen, which should offer some substantial resistance, and 121, probably some more there," said Scott Siller, senior technical analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch.

"Bank of Japan fears will start to materialize soon and the daily studies are starting to diverge bearishly so it looks like this rally should be coming to an end fairly soon at least for corrective weakness," he continued.
For now, the month-long bull trendline, currently at 118.15 yen and rising about 30 ticks per day, remains the key support for dollar/yen.
"If we lose that we get serious about the downside," said Siller.
Dollar/mark hit 1.8913 on Wednesday, its highest since October 1989, before bearish divergence on the short-term charts deflected it, analysts said.
On hourly charts, Monday's top at 1.8735 coincides with short-term trendline support on Wednesday. A loss of that level should promote a quick drop to 1.8675 then 1.8600 marks, analysts said.
But while the studies on longer-term charts are overbought, there are no bearish divergences to point to anything other than a deep but healthy correction.
"In dollar/mark, we can fall down to 1.85 and still be bullish," Spain said.
At 1345 EDT on Wednesday, the dollar was at 1.8830/35 marks, down from 1.8860/70 at the New York open and at 118.84/89 yen down from 119.46/51.
